events.title: Elfscape: Ancestors - developer stream
events.summary: Hey everyone,we've prepared an endless gameplay showcase that loops continuously, allowing visitors to jump in at any time and see the world of Elfscape: Ancestors in action. The footage covers nearly two-thirds of the game's current content, offering a much deeper look at the adventure than we've ever shown before!

events.title: Strong, stubborn, and sleepy
events.summary: Hello!Today, it’s time to meet the other half of our unlikely duo.So, what can we say about Agol?Unlike Jachan, Agol’s heart doesn’t fully belong to Lahmu. It’s not that he rejects devotion — he just tends to be… distracted. Food, sleep, or a passing thought can easily take priority, even in the middle of prayer.Agol is easygoing and loves a good joke, but he’s also impulsive and surprisingly brave. events.title: Quiet, devoted, and in trouble
events.summary: Hello!Today, we’d like to introduce you to one of our two comic protagonists a bit more closely. But don’t worry — we’ll try to do it without giving too much away.So, what can we tell you about Jachan?Well, first of all, he is… quiet. Not just when standing next to Agol — Jachan is simply a shy person by nature. He doesn’t speak much, and when he does, it’s usually carefully considered. But what he lacks in confidence, he makes up for in devotion.Jachan firmly believes that true happiness can on

events.title: Headhunters
events.summary: Hello!Let’s return to the underground city of Eshara where our comic side-story begins with a small, very relatable moment.Agol wakes up late.The temple bells have already sounded, and the morning prayer is underway. For the Unworthy — the name given to the worshippers of the two-faced god Lahmu — this is part of their everyday life. Agol rushes through the city, half-asleep and trying to catch up with the day.The day continues and the story follows two hunters of the Unworthy, Jachan and Agol.

events.title: Balancing the Economy (The Andrej Standard)
events.summary: The game shop is ready to open for business! We’ve spent some time staring at spreadsheets and tweaking numbers, but we’ve finally landed on a pricing structure for skins and items that feels just right. To get the economy balanced, we didn't just throw darts at a board. We put our level designer, Andrej, to work. events.title: Teleporting in practice 101
events.summary: Did you know that you can teleport between the main city and different levels of the game? How, you may ask?It all starts with collecting the occasional god dog’s statue heads in levels. By assembling the head with the rest of the statue, you gain points in your skill tree. Accumulate enough points, and you get a new bonus power! One of these bonus powers is the ability to teleport between levels. events.title: Voices and Vibes
events.summary: Hi everyone! In Elfscape: Ancestors, the gameplay is accompanied by narration from the main character, the Guardian. Her monologues are part of the story - she comments on your progress with helpful tips and shares her thoughts about the in-game events.The Guardian is voiced by the talented Eli Nightingale (https://x.com/EliNightVA) , whose performance helps bring the character to life. She can be proud, she can be bossy, but she’s also enthusiastic and passionate - you’ll love her!🔊Sound on! 🔊

events.title: Spin that statue!
events.summary: Hi! First of all, we want to wish you a happy 2025 and thank you for following our story through the developer diaries. You are the best! :) To start the new year on a light funny note, look at this bug - it’s an unfortunate rotating of the dog god statue: This is what it was originally supposed to work like… :D And good news, this is the last time we wish you a new year through our developer’s diary! This year, Elfscape: Ancestors will be finally finished and published.

events.title: Tune-Tastic Tracks
events.summary: Our soundtrack for Elfscape: Ancestors represents different music styles, from gentle emotional piano to energetic electronic beats. We’ll show you two tracks from the soundtrack album, just to get a taste. The game music is adaptive and responds to the gameplay. It is created in FL Studio, and implemented into the game with the use of middleware Fmod. Sound on! :) This emotional track is featured at the beginning of the game, in the menu. The battle track can be heard during the boss encounters

events.title: Keys or buttons
events.summary: Today we’ll take a look at the current work in progress of our programmer - controls mapping. The preferred and recommended way to play Elfscape: Ancestors is using your gamepad controller, as it will provide you with the best and most balanced experience. However for those of you that don’t have or don’t like gamepads, don’t worry! Of course we are adding the option to use your keyboard, and to remap the game controls as you see fit. events.summary: Welcome back to our dev diary series on level design. Today, we’re discussing the creation of immersive environments. As shown in the images below, lighting is just the beginning. We’re also adding various decorations to make each level unique. From plants and windows to runes and artifacts, these embellishments contribute to the overall scene. events.title: Light 'em up!
events.summary: The current focus in finishing our game is level lighting 💡We have many glowing objects, some are moving, some are static. Rendering in-game lights can be demanding on the computer, so we are compromising between the volume of lights and computer performance. We aim to optimize the lighting in order to spare resources, with the use of the Lights 2D package from Unity.
